steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Peel and quarter potatoes, and introduce into boiling water; cook until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and mash. Set aside.

In a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook ground beef and onion until beef is brown. Drain. Stir in tomato soup and green beans. Pour into a 9x13 baking dish. Mound mashed potatoes in a ring around the meat mixture (do not cover meat). Sprinkle potatoes with shredded cheese.
Bake in preheated oven 30 minutes, until potatoes are golden.

raw_recipe.headline: Hamburger Pie
raw_recipe.description: A ground beef, green bean casserole ringed with mashed potatoes and topped with shredded cheese.

review.reviewBody: I remember this from my mother making it. We use 1 can of mushroom soup and 1 can of tomato soup mixed together. The mushroom soup really adds flavor. I couldn't remember how to make it until I found this recipe and it came back to me. Thank you!!

Loved it! Great recipe to clear out your pantry! I made a few changes but overall it was great. I browned the meat with garlic powder and onions. For the potatoes I used instant because it was what I had on hand (2 packages buttery homestyle, then some sprinkles of regular). I did what someone else suggested and put an egg, garlic and seasoned salt in the potatoes, and I also used cream of mushroom with the tomato soup. I mixed a can of diced tomatoes with garlic, onion and pepper along with a frozen bag of mixed veggies along with the green beans. Added a few squirts of worchester, ketchup, sprinkle of salt and pepper, cheddar and parmesan shredded cheese then mixed the mixture all up and placed it in a pan with the potatoes and cheese on top. SCRUMPTIOUS!

I make this once a week for my family and it makes a great dish to take to a potluck. My recipe is out of the Better Homes ad Gardens New Cookbook on page 245. The differences/substitutions are it only calls for 1 can beans, 1 can of tomato soup and 1/2 cup onion and 3/4 tsp salt & 1/8 tsp pepper. Since this recipe doesn't use any salt pepper it could be the reason some think it is bland. My recipe says to add 1 beaten egg and milk when you mash your potatoes and to make them stiff enough to hold shape so you can drop the potatoes in mounds atop meat mixture sprinkle with cheese. I serve garlic bread as a side. Yummy!!

Made this for dinner last night and my family RAVED! There are four of us and everyone (including the super-picky teenage girl) had seconds. I did use real mashed potatoes, made with butter and whole milk. The flavor of instant just isn't the same and my family complains every time I try to use it. The only substitutions were 1 can tomato soup and 1 can diced tomatoes (because I didn't have 2 cans of soup), undrained. Also, I have an italian spice mix that I threw in a teaspoon(ish) of. I also added a teaspoon(ish) of minced garlic while sauteing. Sea salt and cracked pepper, of course. I tend to always spice things up, so that does not affect how I rate a recipe.

I thought this was great! Here is what I did different: I added one can tomato soup, one can mushroom soup (as suggested), Cavander's Greek seasoning, one can of corn for texture and I added all the mashed potatoes to the top (I used 2 pouches of instant). Cheap, easy and it feed a family of 5 with 2nds to be had plus some left overs.

I really enjoyed this recipe. I used all ingredients but added diced celery, carrots and 1/2 tsp of red pepper flakes sauteed with the onions and ground beef. I had fresh parsley to use up and added that to the mashed potatoes with milk & butter.

Read reviews and decided to go with (1) can cream of mushroom, (1) can cream of tomato which I added to the hamburger, (1) c. peas & (1) c. corn (no green beans) and also added Worcestershire. Had chix stock leftover so cooked potatoes in this (would not do this unless I had it around). Added spices, sour cream as well as milk to the potatoes once mashed. I thought it was great!

I cooked the hamburger with diced onions in a fry pan, drained grease. I didn’t have tomato soup, I used diced tomatoes with liquid it came in, mixed with mixed vegetables, blended together. I had some leftover mashed potatoes I heated in microwave. When serving put the hamburger vegetable mixture, with a couple spoonfuls mashed potatoes on top with some shredded Mexican cheese melting on top.

I used almost two pounds of hamburger. I cooked the diced onion, freshly peeled and diced carrots, and two cloves of minced garlic together. fter adding the soup, I thought it was rather blah, so I added about two tablespoons of worcestershire sauce, some crushed red pepper flakes and some cayenne pepper. The whole family loved it.

I made mashed potatoes with red potatoes, salt, butter and milk. My ground beef was cooked with a cup and a half of small diced onions and a tablespoon of minced garlic. I added a can of condensed tomato soup and 1 can of diced Italian tomatoes. I put it in a 9"x13" glass dish. I then put a layer of steamed corn (i had no french cut green beans like I usually use). I topped it all with the potatoes. Then I added a generous layer of cheddar/Monterey mix. Finally I added French's Onions to the top and baked in the 350 oven for about 25 minutes. ** Result** YUM-O! Kids liked it, hubby liked it and I liked it.

As written this would be very bland. Where are the seasonings? I took the suggestions of others and used one can of tomato and one can of cream of mushroom soup. I seasoned the meat/soup mixture to my taste, and made the mashed potatoes with a little butter and salt as I normally would. Also, I did not mix in the green beans -- I just cooked them as a side dish. Edit: I thought this dish was great with the modifications I made. Also, I wanted to note that I used ground turkey instead of ground beef.
I added green peppers with the onions, and onion powder, garlic powder, salt and pepper - Fantastic!!!
Wonderful comfort food my grandmother used to make. She only used peas. I decided to go with peas and green beans. Next time I might try a can of mixed vegetables.
This turned out better than expected. I added a few seasonings, extra cheese, etc. All in all it was a hit with everyone even the picky eaters.
This is pretty much identical to my mom's hamburger pie recipe from when I was a kid. And I love it. The essence of comfort food. And it has all of your daily vitamins and minerals.

This recipe is an old family favorite. My husband hates it because of green beans but tough! Follow this recipe and you'll love it. I always add a bit of garlic and onion powder. You can spice it as you like. Quick one pan meal that goes great with a green salad.
Brings back childhood memories! Delicious..
Pretty good. I used the mushroom soup, too, and added Worcestershire sauce. I wasn't wow-ed, but it was good. Would I make it again? Not sure.

This come out of one of the women magazines back in the late 70's. My kids loved it too and it was a great way to use leftover mashed potatoes. This is perfect just the way it is. But do your own twist.
Absolutely delicious & vety easy to make! I didnt have much cheddar cheese, so i used the mozzarella cheese.
